A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Domain-RAG work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments across three few-shot tasks, module and retrieval ablations, image-quality measurements and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments varying the retrieval database in Section 4.3, Table 5.

M1.justification: The retrieval, background-generation and foreground-composition procedures remain unchanged, including CLIP/ResNet retrieval, Redux/FLUX conditioning, FLUX-Fill composition and rescaling. The new database experiments test existing components.

E1.justification: v2 Table 5 adds a scenario using industrial NEU-DET images as the retrieval database, extending the COCO/miniImageNet retrieval-source comparison in v1. The detection tasks and target benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The detection and augmentation comparator sets are retained, including GroundingDINO, ETS, Copy-Paste and foreground/background augmentation. The new database rows are Domain-RAG ablations; newly cited methods are not added to reported comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 introduces retrieval-pool settings restricting COCO to 1, 5 or 20 categories alongside the existing full database. The retained experiments keep their shot protocols, detector configurations, training budgets and metrics.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 extends the existing database ablation to test category breadth and general-domain versus industrial retrieval sources. The COCO/miniImageNet comparison already existed in v1 Appendix A.2.1; other ablations, image-quality analyses and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added database results follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 Table 5 adds average scores of 30.9, 31.5 and 32.3 for COCO pools containing 1, 5 and 20 categories, and 31.1 for NEU-DET retrieval. Existing benchmark and appendix results remain unchanged, including COCO's 33.6 and miniImageNet's 32.1.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and Equations 1–6 retain the same mathematical content. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the training-free, model-agnostic generation contribution, foreground-preservation principle and state-of-the-art claims across the same three tasks. The reported headline gains are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations favoring broader category coverage and general-domain retrieval databases, plus a fairness rationale referencing COCO's role in the original closed-source benchmark. Existing explanations of miniImageNet performance, foreground leakage and filtering limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 promises code release upon acceptance; v2 states that source code and instructions are available and supplies a repository link. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters and hardware descriptions are retained.

R1.justification: v2 retains all earlier cited works and adds eleven, including ControlCopy-Paste, EarthSynth, SEEDS and RAG-6DPose. These broaden related-work coverage without substantially revising the paper's novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and typo corrections, updates affiliations and contribution markers, adds the database discussion and acknowledgment, and reformats references. The overall narrative, section sequence and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5, enlarges Figure 2 and adjusts table formatting and placement. Existing figures retain their content, and appendix tables are renumbered without substantive display changes.

improvement.justification: The additional database experiments provide useful evidence about retrieval-source selection and category breadth, while the new code-access statement improves reproducibility information. These are limited gains over an otherwise unchanged method and empirical record. The added study leaves subset construction and statistical uncertainty unspecified, limiting the strength of its conclusions.
